request: why is 80 to 100 a 25% rise but 100 to 80 only a 20% fall?

beats.intent: Two bars, 80 and 100, with the gap of 20 lit
beats.narration: Going from eighty to a hundred adds twenty.
beats.code:
stage.title("Percent change depends on the start")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [80, 100], labels=["80", "100"])
stage.caption("The gap is 20 either way")

beats.intent: The gap 20 compared with 80: a 25% rise
beats.narration: Twenty out of the starting eighty is a quarter: a twenty five percent rise.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[0], color=GREEN)
stage.equation(r"\frac{20}{80} = 25\%")

beats.intent: The same gap compared with 100: a 20% fall
beats.narration: Coming back, the same twenty is measured against a hundred: a twenty percent fall.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, bars[1], color=RED)
stage.equation(r"\frac{20}{100} = 20\%")

request: why can't you just average two averages?

beats.intent: Bars of two classes: 10 students averaging 90 and 30 students averaging 50
beats.narration: One class of ten averages ninety; another of thirty averages fifty.
beats.code:
stage.title("Averaging averages")
bars = draw_bars(stage, [90, 50], labels=["10 students", "30 students"])

beats.intent: A dashed line at 70, the naive average of the two averages
beats.narration: The average of the two averages is seventy.
beats.code: stage.caption("Naive: (90 + 50) / 2 = 70")

beats.intent: A dot grid of 40 students, 10 blue and 30 red, beside the true mean 60
beats.narration: But there are three times as many students in the second class. Counting everyone: ninety times ten plus fifty times thirty, over forty, is sixty.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
dots = draw_dots(stage, n=40, cols=10, color=RED)
stage.play(*[dots[k].animate.set_color(BLUE) for k in range(10)])
stage.equation(r"\frac{10 \cdot 90 + 30 \cdot 50}{40} = 60")

beats.intent: A five-pointed star
beats.narration: Here is a five-pointed star.
beats.code:
stage.title("Rotational symmetry")
star = Star(n=5, outer_radius=2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
stage.play(Create(star))
stage.add(star)
dot = Dot(star.get_vertices()[0], color=RED)
stage.add(dot)

beats.intent: The star turning a fifth of a turn, 72°, and landing on itself
beats.narration: Turn it by seventy two degrees, a fifth of a turn: it looks exactly the same. Only the red point moved.
beats.code: stage.play(Rotate(VGroup(star, dot), TAU / 5, about_point=ORIGIN), run_time=1.5)

beats.intent: The star beside order 5: 360° ÷ 72° = 5
beats.narration: It fits onto itself five times in a full turn: rotational symmetry of order five.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"360^\circ \div 72^\circ = 5")

request: how many lines of symmetry does a square have?

beats.intent: A square
beats.narration: Here is a square.
beats.code:
stage.title("Lines of symmetry")
sq = Square(side_length=3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
stage.play(Create(sq))
stage.add(sq)

beats.intent: The vertical and horizontal mirror lines through the middle
beats.narration: Fold it down the middle either way and the halves match: two lines.
beats.code:
v = DashedLine(UP * 2, DOWN * 2, color=YELLOW)
h = DashedLine(LEFT * 2, RIGHT * 2, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(v), Create(h))
stage.add(v, h)

beats.intent: The two diagonal mirror lines added, four in all
beats.narration: The two diagonals also work, so a square has four lines of symmetry.
beats.code:
d1 = DashedLine(np.array([-2, -2, 0]), np.array([2, 2, 0]), color=GREEN)
d2 = DashedLine(np.array([-2, 2, 0]), np.array([2, -2, 0]), color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(d1), Create(d2))
stage.add(d1, d2)
stage.caption("4 lines of symmetry")

request: what are corresponding and alternate angles?

beats.intent: Two parallel horizontal lines crossed by a slanted transversal
beats.narration: Two parallel lines, crossed by a third line.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angles and parallel lines")
l1 = Line(np.array([-4, 1, 0]), np.array([4, 1, 0]), color=WHITE)
l2 = Line(np.array([-4, -1, 0]), np.array([4, -1, 0]), color=WHITE)
t = Line(np.array([-1.5, -2.5, 0]), np.array([1.5, 2.5, 0]), color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(l1), Create(l2), Create(t))
stage.add(l1, l2, t)

beats.intent: The corresponding angles at the two crossings marked equal in yellow
beats.narration: At each crossing the angle in the same position is equal: corresponding angles.
beats.code:
P1, P2 = np.array([0.6, 1, 0]), np.array([-0.6, -1, 0])
d = np.array([3, 5, 0]) / np.linalg.norm([3, 5])
a1 = Angle(Line(P1, P1 + RIGHT), Line(P1, P1 + d), radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
a2 = Angle(Line(P2, P2 + RIGHT), Line(P2, P2 + d), radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(a1), Create(a2))
stage.add(a1, a2)

beats.intent: An alternate angle below the top line marked equal in green, making a Z
beats.narration: And the angle on the other side of the transversal, under the top line, matches too: alternate angles, in a Z shape.
beats.code:
a3 = Angle(Line(P1, P1 + LEFT), Line(P1, P1 - d), radius=0.5, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(a3))
stage.add(a3)
stage.caption("Corresponding (F) and alternate (Z) angles are equal")

request: what does a bearing of 060° mean?

beats.intent: A compass circle with North at the top
beats.narration: Bearings are measured clockwise from North.
beats.code:
stage.title("Bearings")
c = draw_circle(stage, radius=2)
north = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP * 2.3, buff=0, color=WHITE)
stage.play(GrowArrow(north))
stage.add(north)
stage.label(north, "N", direction=UP)

beats.intent: An arrow turned 60° clockwise from North, the angle marked
beats.narration: Turn sixty degrees clockwise from North.
beats.code:
b = Arrow(ORIGIN, 2.3 * np.array([np.sin(np.radians(60)), np.cos(np.radians(60)), 0]), buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(GrowArrow(b))
stage.add(b)
ang = Angle(Line(ORIGIN, b.get_end()), Line(ORIGIN, UP), radius=0.7, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(ang))
stage.add(ang)

beats.intent: The arrow labelled 060°, with 180° pointing South shown for comparison
beats.narration: That direction is written zero six zero. Due South would be one eight zero.
beats.code:
stage.label(b, "060°", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
s = Arrow(ORIGIN, DOWN * 2.3, buff=0, color=GREY_B)
stage.play(GrowArrow(s))
stage.add(s)
stage.label(s, "180°", direction=DOWN)

request: how do you enlarge a shape by scale factor 2 from a point?

beats.intent: A small triangle and a centre point O
beats.narration: A small triangle, and a centre of enlargement O.
beats.code:
stage.title("Enlargement")
p = draw_plane(stage)
O = mark_point(stage, p, (-3, -2), color=RED, label="O")
tri = Polygon(p.c2p(-2, -1), p.c2p(0, -1), p.c2p(-1, 0.5), color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
stage.play(Create(tri))
stage.add(tri)

beats.intent: Rays from O through each corner, extended to twice the distance
beats.narration: Draw a ray from O through each corner and go twice as far.
beats.code:
for x, y in ((-2, -1), (0, -1), (-1, 0.5)):
    draw_line(stage, p.c2p(-3, -2), p.c2p(-3 + 2 * (x + 3), -2 + 2 * (y + 2)), color=GREY_B, dashed=True)

beats.intent: The enlarged triangle with corners (-1, 0), (3, 0), (1, 3) drawn
beats.narration: Join the new points: the same shape, every length doubled.
beats.code:
big = Polygon(p.c2p(-1, 0), p.c2p(3, 0), p.c2p(1, 3), color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.4)
stage.play(Create(big))
stage.add(big)
stage.caption("Scale factor 2: every length doubles")
